headline: Chicago scrap expected up $10–$40 a ton in November
detail: BL Duke sees all grades rising, with mills trying to hold it to $10–$30; busheling futures are above $500 and yards are thin. October already rose about $30, and the settle should land by Nov 10.

headline: Copper heads for first monthly loss since June
detail: LME three-month copper slid about 1.5% Friday to near $14,130 as an AI and tech selloff hit risk appetite, ending a three-month win streak. COMEX fell to about $6.46, then bounced toward $6.50 Monday.

headline: Copper and brass scrap give back part of a big week
detail: The ScrapMonster index cut clean copper grades 5¢/lb and brass 1¢ on Oct 29, after copper grades gained about 20¢ for the week. Steel and aluminum grades stayed flat, so yard copper bids may ease with Friday's drop.

headline: Gold breaks to a one-year low near $3,875
detail: Gold lost about 3.6% Friday, its lowest since October 2025, on margin selling after the tech rout and on oil-driven rate fears. Silver fell about 6% to near $49, down about 9% on the week.

headline: US hot-rolled steel hits $1,429, highest since 2022
detail: Midwest HRC rose again Friday, up nearly 9% in a month, as 50% tariffs, mill outages and costlier scrap keep supply tight. Strong steel pricing gives mills room to pay more for scrap.

headline: Hormuz tanker attack pushes Brent to about $118
detail: Oil rose over 2% Friday after a tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, adding to inflation and rate worries that hit metals. Monday oil eased on reports of more time for Iran diplomacy.

headline: China's official factory gauge drops to 49.3
detail: The October reading fell from 50.1 and missed the 50.0 forecast, the lowest since July. Contraction in the biggest metals buyer is a headwind for copper and iron ore.

headline: US and Canada push for steel and auto tariff deal
detail: Talks that collapsed in August are moving again, and a limited deal could come around the Nov 3 midterms, though US sources want more concessions. Lower duties on Canadian steel could cool US steel prices.

headline: Fed held rates, but two members wanted a hike
detail: The Fed stayed at 3.75%–4.00% on a 10–2 vote, with September CPI at 3.7% and core PCE at 3.1%. Hike risk in December keeps pressure on metals.

headline: Chile slashes 2026 copper output forecast by 8.4%
detail: Cochilco now sees 4.94 million tons this year and only a small rebound in 2027, with September output down about 15%. It raised its copper price forecasts to $6.18 for 2026 and $5.95 for 2027, which supports prices.

headline: China pays a record premium for copper even as prices fall
detail: The Yangshan import premium topped $200 a ton, and spot LME metal trades over $170 above three-month. Physical supply is tight outside the US, which limits how far prices can drop.

headline: Nucor profit doubles; sees a steady fourth quarter
detail: Q3 net income was $1.32 billion, with average mill prices of $1,233/st and scrap cost of $421 a gross ton. The company expects Q4 flat to modestly higher, a sign of steady scrap demand.

headline: Turkish scrap firms toward $400
detail: LME Turkey scrap futures rose $10 to $401.50 on Oct 29, and Kallanish reported a fresh US deal holding prices firm. Stronger export demand supports obsolete grades like HMS in the US.

headline: Iron ore ends October at its weakest month-end since 2022
detail: Dalian futures sat near four-year lows below 680 yuan as port stocks rose to about 153.7 million tons and Vale's profit fell 20%. Weak ore makes blast-furnace steel cheaper abroad but does little for US scrap.

headline: US aluminum premium at a record as Canadian metal goes to Europe
detail: The 50% US tariff on Canadian aluminum has pushed US prices to a record gap over world prices, while Canada ships more to Europe. That keeps US scrap aluminum values well supported.

headline: Aluminum bucks Friday's slide
detail: LME cash aluminum rose 1.4% to $3,114 while most metals fell, with exchange stocks down to about 231,200 tons, a very low level. Gulf output is still well below pre-war levels.

headline: Nickel slips as Indonesian cut hopes fade
detail: SHFE nickel fell 2.8% on the week as expected cuts lacked firm schedules and Chinese stocks grew 2.1%. Indonesia also cut its ore benchmark by 2.9%, which points to soft stainless scrap.

headline: October US car sales seen at a 16.1 million pace
detail: Cox Automotive expects about 1.38 million sales, up 7.2% from a year ago with an extra selling day. Steady sales mean steady stamping scrap from plants and demand for sheet steel.

headline: Ford lifts its 2026 metal cost estimate to about $2.5 billion
detail: The increase from about $2 billion cites copper and steel, among other costs. Automakers are feeling high metal prices and may push suppliers harder.

headline: Stellantis stops most French plants; Toyota output falls
detail: Four of five French assembly plants halted this month, partly on EV battery shortages, and Toyota's global output fell 3.2% in September. Fewer cars built means less auto demand for steel and PGMs.

headline: Housing starts fell 5.2% in September
detail: Starts dropped to a 1.22 million pace and single-family permits fell 4%. Weaker home building trims demand for copper wire and pipe, aluminum and steel.

headline: Private China factory survey holds up at 52.0
detail: The RatingDog PMI beat the 51.6 forecast and barely slipped from 52.1, a much better read than the official 49.3. The split leaves copper traders unsure how weak China really is.

headline: China mills cut steel output but stocks keep rising
detail: Daily output at large mills fell 2.3% in mid-October to 1.894 million tons, while inventories rose 1.5%. Soft demand limits iron ore and Chinese scrap prices.

headline: Platinum sinks to its lowest since September 2025
detail: Platinum is near $1,434, down about 17% in a month, as outflows and costly fuel weigh on it; the WPIC now sees a 265,000-ounce surplus this year. Lower platinum means lower converter payouts.

headline: Palladium under $1,000; rhodium quote stuck
detail: Palladium closed near $981 after falling about 2.5% Friday, while Kitco's rhodium quote stayed at $8,550 bid and $9,550 ask. Converter yards should expect softer pricing this week.

headline: Refined copper tariff still undecided
detail: The White House has not ruled on a proposed 15% tariff from January 2027, and US-held stocks are expected to stay put until it is dropped. That keeps COMEX and LME prices apart.

headline: Tech rout sends the Nasdaq down 2.9%
detail: Intel's near-30% plunge led Friday's selloff, with the S&P 500 down 1.8% and copper miners down 5–7%. Investors moved to bonds, yet about 70% odds of another hike this year kept metals from benefiting.

headline: Wall Street turns bearish on gold as it bounces
detail: In Kitco's survey 63% of analysts expect lower prices next week, while gold recovered to near $3,906 early Monday. Midterms and Friday's jobs report are the next tests.

headline: LA–Long Beach port strike threat pushed to Nov 5
detail: The watchmen's union and employers extended talks instead of striking Nov 1. A walkout could disrupt container terminals, including scrap and metal shipments.
